patch_description:
The current approach uses 8 perturbed/geometric seeds, 3 sharpness schedules, 1450 surrogate-gradient iterations per trajectory, momentum 0.82, initial step size 0.046, and periodic exact-score checkpointing with restart on regressions. The revised implementation keeps the successful multi-basin continuation stage but changes its schedules, shortens it to 1250 iterations, and adds a final portfolio of exact-monotone contact-polishing branches from the globally best checkpoint.

The new final branches use distinct sharpness ranges (220→650, 320→980, and 500→1450), lower local step sizes, exact evaluation of several line-search candidates at every iteration, and occasional deterministic small perturbation candidates. This separates basin discovery from high-precision active-contact optimization: surrogate dynamics can still cross contact-graph transitions early, while the final stage only retains evaluator-equivalent improvements.
